html:
A Byzantine philosopher who taught at Mistra in the Peloponnese and was the leading follower of Plato in his time. He lived from about 1355 to about 1452 or 1454.

At Mistra he urged the rulers to reform the Morea along lines taken from Plato's Republic. His students included Bessarion.

In 1438 he went with the Greek delegation to the Council of Florence. There, aged over eighty, he lectured to Italian humanists on how Plato differed from Aristotle. Marsilio Ficino later wrote that these talks inspired Cosimo de' Medici to found the Platonic Academy in Florence, which revived Plato in the Renaissance.

His last book, the Laws, sketched a new pagan religion built on the Greek gods. After his death Gennadius Scholarius had it burned, and only fragments survive.
